About the Role We are looking for a software engineer to join our Streaming Systems team, working on the high-throughput systems that collect, forward, and perform real time computation on billions of behavioral events from our customers’ users.

You'll be building the infrastructure that ingests clickstream, product interaction, and transactional data into our platform. This data is the platform for our “Cursor for Marketers” AI agent product. Our streaming products’ revenue has 10x’d over the past year, and we need to ensure that we continue to scale.

Our infrastructure needs to handle millions of messages per second at single second latency end to end. Recently, we added a computation engine that allows personalizing user experiences in real-time based on live behavior; we’re seeing 7-figure market response in the first few months and need to scale up to meet demand.

We believe in enabling our engineers to do their best work for our customers by giving them extremely high levels of ownership and autonomy. You will own and deliver projects from start to finish, work directly with customers to solve their hardest scaling problems, and have significant influence over our technical roadmap.

The base salary range for this position is $180,000 - $320,000 USD per year, which is location independent in accordance with our remote-first policy. A large portion of the compensation will be in the form of equity via ISO options. We offer early exercise and a 10 year post-termination exercise window.

You have experience and comfort with distributed systems and high-scale systems or the ability and desire to build this experience quickly. This experience can take different forms.

eleQtron develops full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Our approach combines laser-cooled ions, microwave and RF control, engineered magnetic field gradients, and advanced theoretical modelling to build scalable quantum processors. In this role, you will contribute to the development of a next-generation Deep Digital Twin software for trapped-ion quantum computers. You will work at the intersection of quantum technologies, numerical simulation, scientific computing, and software engineering, developing predictive models that connect microscopic physical processes to system-level performance metrics.
A key component of the position is transforming and extending existing research-grade simulation tools into a robust, scalable, and maintainable software framework. These tools will support hardware design, control optimization, system characterization, performance benchmarking, and the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.
The Deep Digital Twin is envisioned as a multi-scale simulation framework spanning several layers of abstraction, from ion trapping, control fields, and noise processes, through quantum state preparation and laser cooling to gate dynamics and reasout, ultimately interfacing with circuit-level simulators and quantum error correction workflows.
You will collaborate closely with theorists, experimental physicists, software developers, and engineers to ensure consistency between physical models, numerical simulations, and experimental observations.

What We’re Building

Honeycomb is a service for the near and present future, defining observability and raising expectations of what developer tools can do! We’re working with well known companies like HelloFresh, Slack, LaunchDarkly, and Vanguard and more across a range of industries. This is an exciting time in our trajectory, we’ve closed Series D funding, scaled past the 200-person mark, and were named to Forbes’ America’s Best Startups of 2022 and 2023!
If you want to see what we’ve been up to, please check out these blog posts and Honeycomb .io press releases.
Who We Are
We come for the impact, and stay for the culture! We’re a talented, opinionated, passionate, fiercely inclusive, and responsible group of bees. We have conviction and we strive to live our values every day. We want our people to do what they truly love amongst a team of highly talented (but humble) peers.
How We Work
We are a fully distributed company, which means we believe it is not where you sit, but how you deliver that matters most. We invest in our people and care about how you orient to our culture and processes. At the same time we imbue a lot of trust, autonomy, and accountability from Day 1.

The LLM Observability (LLM O11y) team builds the foundational layer that makes AI workloads observable in Honeycomb .

We define how AI systems are represented in telemetry (spans, traces, token usage, cost, eval signals, etc), and ensure that data from diverse ecosystems (e.g., LangChain, OpenLLMetry, Braintrust) is normalized into a consistent OpenTelemetry-based model.

This team owns the infrastructure and data model that all downstream AI observability experiences rely on. Our work powers everything from cost analysis to anomaly detection. If you’re excited about defining and building the “source of truth” for how AI systems behave in production, this is the team for you.

s.h: What you’ll do in the role
s.t:
Design, build, and deliver backend systems and APIs. You'll architect and implement APIs and backend services in Go, emphasizing clarity, maintainability, and backward compatibility. You'll think proactively about cost, scale, and risk — anticipating technical issues and exploring alternatives and tradeoffs thoroughly.

Build and maintain full-stack product features. You'll contribute frontend (React/TypeScript) and backend (Go) code to build robust product features, maintaining proficiency across the stack. You'll deliver impactful features that add value for our customers, our team, and Honeycomb overall.

Provide technical leadership. You'll define patterns and operational guidelines that raise the bar for the team and beyond. You'll plan, lead, and deliver complex, multi-team projects — including ones with external dependencies — ensuring alignment and mentoring teammates along the way. We rotate tech lead responsibilities with each feature to allow everyone on the team to use and grow these skills.

Collaborate across disciplines. You'll work closely within a product triad model alongside design and product partners, from discovery through delivery, iterating quickly based on user feedback. You'll contribute to the team's technical roadmap and help shape quarterly product roadmaps, tying technical considerations to business outcomes.

Support and own your software in production. You'll participate in on-call rotations to ensure reliable operations and proactively address user pain points. You know when to shift between forward-looking feature work and production needs.

Communicate clearly and multiply your impact. Regular written and verbal communication, collaboration, and feedback are foundational skills you'll use daily. You'll mentor engineers, share knowledge, and delegate to help others grow — your goal is to make everyone around you more effective.

s.h: What you’ll bring to the role
s.t:
Deep experience designing, building, and maintaining backend systems. You have substantial expertise building APIs and backend services in Go (or similar languages), with strong opinions about API design, error handling, and developer experience. You've seen many different patterns and have developed your own frameworks for evaluating how to approach new technical challenges.

Frontend proficiency with React and TypeScript. You have professional experience delivering frontend features and contributing to full-stack software through all stages of the development lifecycle, though your primary expertise is in backend systems.

Experience leading complex technical projects. You've planned and delivered projects that span multiple teams or systems, navigating external dependencies and uncertainty. You know how to break down complex work, ship incrementally, and balance technical investment with business goals.

Ownership and autonomy. You proactively identify problems, propose solutions, and own your projects end-to-end — from planning through deployment and ongoing maintenance. You tackle tech debt proactively and can debug the toughest issues through the entire stack.

A track record of making others better. You've mentored engineers, led technical design reviews, and helped raise the quality bar for a team or domain. People come to you for guidance, and you help build leaders around you.

A collaborative and flexible mindset. You're comfortable working cross-functionally, pivoting priorities to address evolving customer or business needs, and maintaining strong teamwork. We work by building small changes and iterating based on customer interaction.

Clear, open communication. We see clear, thoughtful, and regular written and face-to-face communication — including a willingness to give and receive feedback — as a fundamental engineering skill and one of the strongest predictors of engineering impact, not just a nice to have, and we hope you do too.

An interest in observability and production culture. We maintain an on-call rotation and work hard to keep it from becoming a bad experience. You've supported software in production and have opinions about how to do it well. Bonus points if you want to fold that experience into the Honeycomb product itself.

Nice to have: experience with AI-assisted development. You're proficient with AI coding tools (Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) or are excited to incorporate them into your workflow. We're actively exploring how AI can accelerate our development practices.

Company Description
Redzone is the #1 Connected Workforce Solution for manufacturers big and small. We work to improve efficiency in plants, provide coaching for best practices, and enable the front-line worker to improve the quality of their work and their work life by providing them with tools, processes, and collaboration tools to keep their manufacturing lines running smoothly and efficiently.
At Redzone we focus on the customer experience, listening to the customer, and providing solutions that create great outcomes. We are a combination of great leadership, years of manufacturing experience, and an incredible technology team that all work together to create great products.
This role is fully remote.
Job Description
ChampionAI is QAD | Redzone agentic platform, purpose-built for manufacturing and utilized by the various business units within QAD | Redzone. This engineer joins the core platform team with three main areas of focus: building new capabilities into the platform, helping Applied AI teams at partner business units build and ship Champions correctly, and directly building Champion agents for business-unit use cases when needed.
You will work in the same codebase as the Applied AI engineers you support, which keeps the enablement work
practical and the platform work focused on real problems.

Platform Development
Build and ship features across the Champion platform repositories
Improve developer experience: tooling, scaffolding, internal documentation, and onboarding paths for Applied AI engineers.
Maintain and evolve the MCP tool server and agent infrastructure that BU teams depend on.
Identify and address friction points that slow down Champion development or deployment
Applied AI Enablement
Support BU Applied AI engineers in building, deploying, and operating Champions correctly
Review agent implementations for prompt quality, scope enforcement, auth configuration, and deployment setup
Contribute to internal engineering guides and skill documentation
Pair with BU engineers on first K8S manifest creation, database registration, and LaunchDarkly prompt rollout
Agent Development
Design and build Champion agents for BU use-cases when the platform team is directly engaged
Write and iterate on system prompts, tool bindings, and context injection for production agents
Register agents in Champion Server and configure LaunchDarkly-gated prompt rollout across environments
Engineering Practices
We follow trunk-based development with PR-gated merges to main. Engineers are expected to:
Write tests before implementing. TDD is the expectation, not a nice-to-have.
Keep PRs small and focused; use feature flags to ship partial work incrementally
Follow conventional commit format (feat:, fix:, etc.)
Be mindful of API and schema backward-compatibility; prefer additive changes over breaking ones
Review your own diff before requesting review

Python: Proficient in async Python, Pydantic, type hints, and FastAPI. Experience with the Strands agent SDK or a comparable agentic framework. Testing is non-optional: candidates should be comfortable with pytest, pytest- asyncio, and DeepEval for agent-specific evaluation. We test agent behavior, not just unit logic.
Prompt Engineering: Able to write and iterate on production system prompts: XML-structured, scope-enforced, with tool descriptions that guide LLM delegation reliably.
Model Context Protocol (MCP): Solid understanding of MCP and hands-on experience building or consuming MCP servers. Familiarity with Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is a strong plus.
Agent Patterns: Familiar with multi-agent architectures and orchestration patterns beyond basic ReAct: supervisor/subagent delegation, parallel tool use, handoffs, and context management across agent boundaries.
Agent Evals: Able to design and run evaluation suites for agent behavior: correctness checks, scope enforcement tests, regression coverage, and systematic prompt iteration based on eval results.
Docker: Comfortable authoring Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, and local dev environments via docker-compose / make.
PostgreSQL: Comfortable with templated INSERT/SELECT, foreign key relationships, and reading an ER diagram.
Git / Semantic Versioning: Follows conventional commit format (feat:, fix:) and a PR-based trunk workflow.

Kubernetes: Working knowledge of Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and ServiceAccounts. Able to read and adapt K8s manifests and use kubectl for basic troubleshooting.
AWS: Working knowledge of ECR, EKS, IAM, and Bedrock (inference layer).
OAuth2 / OIDC: Conceptual understanding of Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, token exchange, and agent auth delegation.
Terraform: Beginner-level familiarity; able to make targeted changes to existing modules and interpret a plan diff.
LaunchDarkly: Experience managing feature flags or AI config overrides for environment-gated rollout.
Document Intelligence / OCR: AWS Textract or comparable pipeline experience for use cases involving structured document extraction.
AI-Native Development
We run an AI-native SDLC. AI-assisted tools (Claude Code, Cursor) are part of the standard engineering workflow at every stage: planning, implementation, review, and documentation. This is not optional or supplemental; it is how we work. Candidates should be comfortable with AI-assisted development and willing to invest in getting good at it.
Use Claude Code and Cursor actively across planning, implementation, and code review
Know when AI output is wrong and push back on it.

Junior Webentwickler (m/w/d) – Quereinsteiger willkommen!
Deine Karrierechance wartet. Werde Teil unseres Teams.
Über uns. Warum wir?
Die ATZ Group , gegründet 1973, verbindet Erfahrung mit Innovationsgeist. Unser Team aus Spezialisten entwickelt digitale Lösungen in den Bereichen Media, Marketing, Recruiting und Intelligence. Gemeinsam mit Partnern aus dem Mittelstand und internationalen Konzernen gestalten wir digitale Projekte und Erfolgsgeschichten weltweit.
Was uns besonders macht: Wir sind vielleicht das älteste Startup der Welt . Seit Jahrzehnten entwickeln wir uns weiter, probieren Neues aus und arbeiten mit modernen Technologien. Bei uns findest du keine starren Strukturen, sondern ein Umfeld, in dem Ideen, Motivation und Weiterentwicklung wirklich zählen.
Wenn du Lust hast, Dinge zu bauen, Technik wirklich zu verstehen und dich dabei in mehrere Richtungen weiterzuentwickeln, bist du bei uns richtig.
Deine Mission 🚀
Du hast Spaß daran, Websites technisch umzusetzen, und du schreckst auch nicht zurück, wenn mal etwas anderes Technisches zu tun ist. Bei uns liegt der Schwerpunkt auf der Webentwicklung, aber die Stelle ist bewusst etwas breiter angelegt. Mal baust du ein Frontend, mal hilfst du einer Kollegin bei einem technischen Problem, mal schaust du, warum eine WordPress-Seite klemmt.
Du bist also kein reiner Entwickler, der nur im Code sitzt, und auch kein klassischer IT-Supporter. Eher ein technischer Allrounder mit klarem Fokus auf Web. Wer gerne versteht, wie Dinge zusammenhängen, und nicht nur an einer einzigen Sache schraubt, fühlt sich hier wohl.
Vielleicht hast du dir vieles selbst beigebracht, erste Webprojekte umgesetzt oder einfach eine große Begeisterung für moderne Webtechnologien. Bei uns baust du dein Wissen aus und tauchst Schritt für Schritt tiefer in Webentwicklung, Softwarelogik und IT-Prozesse ein.

✔ Webentwicklung als Schwerpunkt
Du entwickelst moderne Frontends für Websites und Landingpages auf Basis bestehender Designs, setzt Projekte technisch um und entwickelst sie weiter. Responsive Layouts mit sauberem HTML und CSS gehören dazu, ebenso JavaScript für interaktive Funktionen und dynamische Inhalte.
✔ WordPress und CMS
Du arbeitest mit WordPress, pflegst Inhalte, aktualisierst Plugins und setzt Anpassungen sowie neue Seiten um. Mit der Zeit lernst du Themes, Templates und Seitenstrukturen im Detail kennen und kannst im Code nachschauen, wenn etwas nicht läuft.
✔ APIs und Funktionalität
Du bindest APIs und externe Services ein, entwickelst Formulare, dynamische Elemente und funktionale Komponenten und hilfst dabei, die Performance und eine saubere Codebasis im Blick zu behalten.
✔ Technische Unterstützung im Team
Wenn Kolleginnen und Kollegen ein technisches Problem haben, bist du ansprechbar. Das reicht von Fragen rund um Tools und Zugänge bis hin zu kleineren Hürden im Arbeitsalltag. Du musst nicht alles sofort können, aber du gehst die Dinge an und findest Lösungen.
✔ IT- und Systemthemen
Du bekommst Einblick in allgemeine IT-Themen wie Webhosting, Domains und technische Systemstrukturen und hilfst mit, verschiedene Tools und Plattformen sinnvoll zu verbinden. So wächst du nach und nach über die reine Entwicklung hinaus.
✔ Fehleranalyse und Optimierung
Wenn etwas nicht funktioniert, gehst du strukturiert vor: Problem eingrenzen, Lösungen recherchieren, Fehler beheben. Ob in einer Website, einem Tool oder einem Setup.
✔ Moderne Technologien
Du hast die Möglichkeit, mit Technologien wie React, Next.js oder Tailwind CSS zu arbeiten und dich dort weiterzuentwickeln.
✔ Zusammenarbeit
Du arbeitest eng mit den Teams aus Marketing, IT, Design und Content zusammen.
Dein Profil. Was du mitbringst 💡

In its journey to become the most loved payment service provider in Europe, Mollie is continuously investing and growing its Engineering department. We recently successfully launched an Engineering Hub in Lisbon and we are set to replicate this journey in one of the most vibrant cities in Europe: Milan!
Milan’s hub will contribute to Mollie’s mission with multiple passionate agile engineering teams that will innovate, build and contribute to our portfolio of next-generation payment products. Our focus is on creating highly scalable solutions that can handle a high volume of payments per second throughout the day. Code quality and system scalability are of paramount importance, and we value forward-thinking experts who can contribute to building scalable systems.
As a Full Stack Engineer II you’ll be a vital part of our Customer Onboarding domain, where we are dedicated to crafting seamless end-to-end onboarding experiences for our customers.

Our focus includes optimizing front-end customer experiences, streamlining data collection and verification processes, managing effective customer communications throughout the onboarding journey. We are committed to making it as effortless as possible for businesses to integrate Mollie into their operations and thrive.

Our mission includes delivering a well-regulated onboarding experience, leveraging intelligent risk decision-making, and maintaining world-class operational capabilities.
What you’ll be doing
You will be part of a small team focused on solving clearly defined problem spaces.
Helping us build large scale systems
Work closely with engineers and product in order to build features at large scale
Work with UI engineers from other teams to maintain consistency and share knowledge
Design, build and maintain APIs, user interfaces, services and systems across Mollie’s engineering teams
Analyse and solve complex problems across the stack
What you will bring
Good communication and collaboration skills, we value this the most out of all the things listed here
Minimum of 5 years experience with developing full-stack web applications, preferably using PHP/MySQL stacks, in combination with modern Javascript frameworks like React, Vue or Angular
Experience with continuous deployment or continuous integration
Knowledge of modern queueing and caching systems like RabbitMQ, Redis, or Kafka
A knack for reducing system complexity, solving cross-team problems, and for striking the right balance between quality and moving fast
You enjoy being a generalist, working on frontend, backend, as needed to solve problems and delight our users
Our engineering workflow
'Ship early, ship often' is our philosophy. We like to break up big challenges into smaller ones, deploying gradual product iterations and improvements numerous times every day.
We uphold code quality through thorough and cooperative peer reviews, CI/CD build pipelines, and gradual feature roll-outs. In other words, we do everything to make sure you feel comfortable pushing your changes to production on a daily basis.
Our architecture
We come from a monolithic background, with our core systems being written in PHP and Java. As our company started to scale up rapidly, we have scaled our infrastructure along with it by employing queueing systems, service oriented and serverless architecture. For current and future services, we use languages like Java as well.
Mollie’s frontend landscape consists of multiple apps, and each application has its own setup, which is optimised for the app’s purpose. Think of our merchant dashboard, API documentation, mobile apps, etc.
In general, our apps are written using TypeScript, in React. We work with flexible and reusable components, have an extensive UI library that we maintain internally, and are always looking for parts of the codebase that we can open-source and share with the community.

We are a 100% remote company with 1,600+ team members across 40+ countries, and we’re backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in Spain, Sweden, UK, Ireland or Germany.

Software Engineer - Synthetic Monitoring The Opportunity: The Synthetic Monitoring squad builds and operates Grafana Cloud Synthetic Monitoring, used by teams globally to proactively verify that their critical user journeys, APIs, and services work as expected - before their customers notice they don't.

Synthetic Monitoring is a multi-tenant distributed system implemented in Go, running on Kubernetes across all major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure), executing billions of synthetic tests each month from probe locations around the world and from customer-operated private probes.

The product is in a scale phase, and our focus is on making Synthetic Monitoring a deeply integrated part of Grafana Cloud: connecting checks to real user experience and cross-product investigation workflows, making check results a trusted signal for AI-assisted workflows, and enabling large organizations to operate the product at enterprise scale on our infrastructure and on their own private probes.

The role is full-stack in the real sense: the same engineer who designs how a check execution flows through scheduling, probes, and the telemetry pipeline should also be able to build the workflow that lets a user understand and act on the result.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software.

We are looking for Software Engineers who are passionate about building reliable systems and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Our stack is Golang, Typescript and React, but we build tools for people using many other stacks.

What you'll be doing: As a Software Engineer on the Synthetic Monitoring squad, you will work across the whole system - Go services and agents on the backend, a TypeScript/React application on the frontend and you'll be expected to reason about it as one system, not two halves. Specifically, you will:

Own features end-to-end across the stack : from API and data model design in Go, through the execution pipeline, to the user-facing workflows in TypeScript/React

Design and evolve systems, not just features : contribute to architectural decisions on scheduling, probe lifecycle, telemetry ingestion, and API design that shape how the product scales

Build the cross-product and AI-assisted workflows that connect Synthetic Monitoring to the wider Grafana Cloud platform

Make the product operable at enterprise scale : the governance and organization primitives that let teams with hundreds of checks manage Synthetic Monitoring as code and with confidence

Break down complex, ambiguous problems into incremental deliverables and iterate quickly based on feedback

Ensure quality through testing, observability of your own systems, and documentation : our checks are something customers alert on, so reliability is a feature

Be a part of the team's on-call rotation and take ownership of the services you're running
We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction.

We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. Technologies you'll work with:
Go (backend services, APIs, and the synthetic monitoring agent)
TypeScript / React (the Synthetic Monitoring app in Grafana)
Kubernetes across AWS, GCP, and Azure
k6 (the execution engine behind scripted and browser checks)
Grafana ecosystem (Mimir, Loki, Prometheus)

s.h: What Makes You a Great Fit
s.t:
You are comfortable working in a remote-first company ; communication is key.
For us, working together means being collaborative, friendly, kind, and respectful . We operate by consensus. You can contribute to a discussion, disagree constructively, and commit to the team's decision. You are able to communicate design decisions clearly in written and spoken English.

Strong Go, or a path to it. We build Synthetic Monitoring in Go. Deep experience building and operating production backend systems in another systems language (Rust, Java, C++) translates well; backend experience limited to JavaScript/Node.js runtimes does not.

Operational mindset. You've run what you've built: you've owned production services, understand what it means to carry a pager, and treat reliability and toil reduction as part of the product.
You are a systems thinker : you reason about how components interact - data flow, failure modes, cost, and operational behavior - not just how a single feature works in isolation.

Pragmatism and short feedback loops. You break complex problems into increments: analyze, design, deliver an MVP, learn, iterate. You are able to design a solution, get feedback, and write a prototype by yourself - the ability to work on your own is crucial.
You have a good understanding of a software development process that takes a user-centered approach . You easily build an understanding of the users' context and goals which will help you build the right solution with the maximum value.
You use AI tools as a natural part of your engineering workflow - whether for accelerating exploration, code review, or reasoning through design tradeoffs - and you're thoughtful about where they help and where they don't.

Core Equity — Owns the foundational logic that powers Ledgy ’s equity engine. Every equity-related event — such as issuing shares, creating new pools, or adjusting ownership — generates transactions. s.t:
You'll work with HelloFresh's GenAI Enablement Squad , a cross-functional team helping teams across the company unlock the practical value of AI. The mission is simple: identify high-impact problems, build AI-powered solutions that solve them, and scale what works.

As a Staff Engineer, you'll work at the intersection of engineering, product, and business.

One week you might be embedded with the HR or Finance teams understanding how they work; the next you'll be building an agentic workflow, integrating it into the internal tooling, or scaling a successful prototype into a production system used across the company.
This is a highly hands-on role. You'll work on problems from discovery to production, working directly with engineers, product managers, and non-technical stakeholders. Rather than waiting for requirements, you'll help define them—identifying where AI can create real leverage and shipping solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes.
While you'll support and advise other engineers and influence technical direction, your primary impact comes from building products people actually use.

SugarAI is redefining CRM for the age of AI.
We’re delivering on the original promise of CRM—turning fragmented customer and revenue signals into clear, prioritized action. Instead of more dashboards or surface-level insights, we help teams focus on what matters most and know exactly what to do next.
More than two decades after our founding, we’re entering a new chapter with clarity and momentum—building intelligent, intuitive solutions that work within the flow of how teams actually sell and serve. We’re focused on solving complex, real-world challenges where relationships, context, and precision make all the difference.
Our global team is united by a shared commitment to impact, ownership, and continuous growth. We create an environment where thoughtful ideas move quickly, where people are trusted to lead, and where flexibility supports how great work gets done.
If you’re excited to help shape what’s next in AI-driven CRM—and build technology that drives real outcomes—we’d love to meet you.

SugarAI ships AI-powered selling and sales intelligence products in a market that moves faster every day. This is not a role for someone who favors traditional software development, or is curious about AI-assisted development and plans to explore it.

It's a role for someone who already works this way who writes clear, machine-readable specifications that feed the agentic development system, uses agentic development tools as standard equipment, and applies genuine critical judgment to what these tools produce before it ships.

You'll build systems and features that power real customer outcomes in a B2B SaaS platform at scale, and you'll do it inside a delivery model where human judgment is the differentiating input, not the bottleneck.
If you want to work on meaningful software with teammates who hold the bar high on both speed and craft, this role is for you.

Bei Conceptboard bauen wir ein Kollaborationsprodukt, auf das Enterprise-Kunden, öffentliche Institutionen und sicherheitskritische Organisationen täglich vertrauen. Damit die Teams, die dieses Produkt entwickeln, jederzeit auf voller Geschwindigkeit liefern können, brauchen sie eine Plattform, die ihnen aus dem Weg geht – nicht eine, die sie ausbremst.
Als Platform Architect / Staff Engineer bist du Eigentümer der Core Platform Architecture – und du baust sie selbst, hands-on. Dein Design-Constraint Nummer eins: Die Plattform ist nie der Bottleneck. Du denkst in Self-Service-Capabilities, sauberen Contracts und klaren Boundaries – und du machst das Platform-Team zum Agentic-Engineering-Lighthouse der gesamten Organisation. Das hier ist keine Ivory-Tower-Rolle: Du setzt Richtung, indem du sie shippst.
Your Responsibilities Target Architecture ownen. Du formulierst, validierst und entwickelst die Architecture der Core Platform – inklusive der make-or-break Entscheidungen dahinter. Du bist die primäre Ansprechperson für Architektur-Ownership auf Platform-Ebene und entlastest damit die bestehende Architektur-Verantwortung von einer einzelnen Person.
Hands-on bauen. Du leitest und trägst persönlich zum Proof-of-Concept bei, der die kritischen Hypothesen validiert – und danach zu den Platform Services selbst. Du bist Builder, nicht nur Designer.
Platform as a Product. Du designst Services als Self-Service-Capabilities, die Module-Teams unblocked halten. Thinnest viable Platform beats Gold-Plating, immer.
Contracts & Standards setzen und schützen. Du definierst und sicherst die Contracts zwischen Plattform und Module-Teams: APIs, Boundaries, Non-Functional Requirements – und sorgst dafür, dass sie eingehalten werden.
Agentic-First von Tag eins. Du etablierst disziplinierte Agentic-Engineering-Practices im Platform-Team und machst es zur Referenz für die gesamte Engineering-Organisation.
Lead by Example. Du inspirierst dein Team mit einem Platform-First-Mindset. Deine Teammitglieder wachsen, weil sie dir zuschauen – und weil du die Standards, die du setzt, selbst lebst.
Alignment mit dem Architect. Du arbeitest eng mit dem bestehenden Architect zusammen, um übergreifende Architektur-Entscheidungen abzustimmen und zu validieren.
Dein Profil Must-haves
Hands-on Builder mit starkem Track Record. Du hast Plattformen oder Services at scale architektiert und gebaut – und du codest noch. Kein reiner Architecture-by-PowerPoint-Hintergrund.
Platform-as-a-Product-Instinct. Du hast Self-Service-Plattformen gebaut, die andere Teams schneller gemacht haben. Du weißt, wie Plattformen zum Bottleneck werden – und designst aktiv dagegen. Interne Teams sind für dich echte Kunden.
Sound Engineering Practices. Testing, Contracts, Observability, CI/CD, klare Boundaries – und das Urteilsvermögen, welche Non-Functional Requirements tatsächlich zählen.
Genuine Motivation für Agentic Engineering. Du willst Agentic-First mit Disziplin bauen, nicht mit Hype – und du willst es für andere modellieren.

Worum es geht
Wir bauen myScribe – eine KI-gestützte Dokumentationslösung, die Ärztinnen und Ärzten den Rücken freihalten soll, damit sie sich wieder auf das konzentrieren können, wofür sie eigentlich Medizin studiert haben: Patientinnen und Patienten. Dazu kommt myScribe Connect, mit dem wir unsere Lösung tief in die Krankenhaus-IT integrieren.
Klingt nach Mission? Ist es auch. Aber wir sind kein Pitch-Deck – wir sind ein Produktteam, das jeden Tag echten Code in echte Kliniken bringt.
Wo wir gerade stehen
myScribe läuft heute dort, wo die Ärzt\*innen arbeiten: On-Prem, in der Klinik-IT, bei zahlenden Kunden in der DACH-Region. Trotzdem releasen wir mehrmals pro Woche – Continuous Deployment, Fix-Forward, ohne Wartungsfenster-Drama. Im Gesundheitswesen? Eher unüblich.
Doch der Markt verschiebt sich: KI-Inferenz wird teuer, Kunden öffnen sich für die Cloud, SaaS rückt in den Fokus. Um diesen Wandel – und alles, was noch kommt – aktiv mitzugestalten, bauen wir gerade das Core-Entwicklungsteam auf, das myScribe durch die nächsten Jahre trägt. Sei dabei.
Aufgaben
Du entwickelst end-to-end an unserem Produkt mit – von der API bis zur UI, vom Konzept bis ins Deployment. Du denkst in Features, nicht in Tickets. Du verstehst, warum eine Funktion gebaut wird, und entscheidest mit, wie sie am besten umgesetzt wird. Wenn etwas in Produktion bricht, willst du wissen, warum – und es dann richtig fixen.
Konkret arbeitest du an unserem .NET-Backend und unseren TypeScript-Frontends, baust und betreust Docker-Container und entwickelst unsere CI/CD-Pipeline weiter.
Du baust mit am SaaS-Stack, der gerade entsteht – Multi-Tenancy, Cloud-Deployment, Skalierung.
Und du arbeitest an den Integrationen, die uns einzigartig machen: FHIR, ISiK, KIS-Anbindungen.
Wie wir arbeiten
Wir sind AI-native. Agentische Coding-Tools wie Claude Code und Cursor sind für uns kein Experiment, sondern Teil des täglichen Werkzeugkastens. Wir erwarten, dass du solche Tools bereits produktiv einsetzt und ihre Stärken und Grenzen aus eigener Erfahrung kennst.
Wir testen, reviewen und refactorn, weil das der einzige Weg ist, dauerhaft schnell zu bleiben. „Quick & Dirty" ist bei uns keine Tugend – aber Prozess um des Prozesses willen auch nicht. Eine Idee am Montag, ein erster Rollout später in der Woche ist normal, nicht die Ausnahme. Kein Scrum-Theater, aber klare Verantwortlichkeiten.
Qualifikation
Mindestens 5 Jahre professionelle Erfahrung als Fullstack-Entwickler:in mit .NET (C#) und TypeScript in Produktionsumgebungen (gerne mit React, Angular oder Vue – wir streiten uns nicht über Frameworks, sondern entscheiden pragmatisch)
Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (C1 oder besser) – unsere Domäne ist das deutsche Gesundheitswesen, und du kommunizierst täglich mit deutschsprachigen Kunden und Kolleg:innen
DevOps-Kenntnisse: Docker ist Pflicht, Erfahrung mit Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Azure oder vergleichbarem ist ein dickes Plus. Erfahrung mit SaaS-Architekturen und Multi-Tenancy ist hochwillkommen
Erfahrung mit Cloud Development und Cloud-Infrastrukturen (z. B. AWS, perspektivisch auch andere Cloud-Plattformen) – insbesondere im Hinblick auf skalierbare und moderne SaaS-Architekturen ein klarer Pluspunkt
Souveräner Umgang mit agentischen Coding-Tools – du kennst ihre Stärken und Grenzen aus eigener Erfahrung
Ein echtes Qualitätsverständnis: Tests, Code Reviews, sauberes Refactoring sind für dich kein Overhead, sondern die Grundlage dafür, schnell liefern zu können
Ownership im besten Sinne: Du übernimmst Verantwortung für das, was du baust – inklusive Betrieb und Monitoring

Einen Healthcare-Background. Den lernst du bei uns. Wichtiger ist, dass du Lust hast, dich in eine komplexe Domäne reinzudenken – und dort wirklich Spuren zu hinterlassen.

At Netflix , our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology.

Come be a part of what’s next. We launched a new ad-supported tier in November 2022 and are building an in-house world-class ad tech ecosystem to offer our members more choices in consuming their content.

Our new tier allows us to attract new members at a lower price point while also creating a compelling path for advertisers to reach deeply engaged audiences. Our Team The Ads Engineering team at Netflix is dedicated to creating a world-class advertising ecosystem that drives our advertising business.

This team's mission is to develop advanced technology that ensures exceptional experiences for both our members and advertisers. Our responsibilities encompass a broad spectrum of products, ranging from sales and media planning to optimizing advertiser outcomes and execution.

This includes inventory and order management, campaign execution, ad serving, audience and identity management, measurement, reporting, and finance.

We use several Netflix investments and innovations - a unique mix of client and server-side ad insertions, state-of-the-art content delivery systems, ad encoding recipes, content understanding, and metadata, etc. We deliver ads in a manner that’s thoughtful of our member’s viewing experience and drive great outcomes for advertisers.

We also ensure that advertiser brand safety is ensured during serving so that members only see the most appropriate ads for them. Our team is faced with the enormous ambitions of building highly performant advertising systems and delivering high impact to our business by monetizing our incredible slate of content.

As one of the newest entrants in the Connected TV advertising space that’s rapidly growing, we seek to build unique value propositions that help us differentiate us and become a market leader in record time.

Our roles come with expectations of delivering in a rapid clip, comfort with lofty goals and big ambitions, the visibility that comes with strategic initiatives, and responsibility and an appetite to operate like a startup within an established company.

We are looking for engineers to join us on this journey, to be a part of some exciting initiatives, and the talented teams who work on realizing our ambitious vision. Skills & experience we’re seeking:
Well grounded domain experience in any of the following areas: Ad Serving, Ads Identity & Audiences, Ads Creatives, Inventory & Forecasting, Campaign Management, Media Planning, Measurement, Reporting, or Ads Finance.
General understanding of the advertising marketplace and landscape.
Worked closely with ad operations to enable campaign setup, targeting, reporting and advertiser needs.
Developed many cloud based applications and comfortable with modern programming languages (preferably object oriented),
Familiar with A/B testing and experimentation.
Have solid experience in setting technical directions for engineering projects, making architectural decisions, and influencing partner and cross-functional teams.

Contributed to an ads industry technology standard (e.g VAST, OpenRTB) or worked on an industry consortium effort, working group etc.
Familiarity with legal compliance and changing landscape of ads regulations around the world.
Experience working in the CTV space and knowledge of it’s unique constraints
Spotlight on Ads Engineering Teams: The Ad Supply team manages the policies and technical integrations for third-party ad supply. While Netflix has traditionally licensed content, we're exploring this alternative funding model.

The team solves complex challenges, such as determining how both Netflix and the third-party partner can sell ad inventory for the same content without conflict. They establish clear rules for inventory sharing, campaign setup, and system configurations to ensure consistency and fairness.

The Ads Measurement team builds systems that enable advertisers on Netflix to quantify campaign outcomes. Leveraging a blend of Netflix innovations and both first-party and third-party solutions, we deliver ads that respect the viewing experience while driving impactful results for advertisers.

Our tools empower advertisers to effectively measure and analyze these outcomes. The Ads Identity and Audience team is dedicated to delivering a relevant and engaging advertising experience while prioritizing consumer privacy.

Our mission is to maintain precise subscriber identities to ensure that ads are not only engaging but also respectful of consumer privacy choices and regional regulations.

We maintain a high-quality Identity Graph, which is used for various purposes, including respecting privacy choices and regulations, audience onboarding, targeting, measurement, and reporting.

The Ads Creatives & Policy team at Netflix is at the forefront of developing innovative solutions that enhance the ad experience for both viewers and advertisers. We are responsible for managing the lifecycle of ad creatives, ensuring compliance with policies, and leveraging cutting-edge technology to optimize ad delivery.

Joining our team means being part of a dynamic environment where your contributions directly impact the viewing experience of millions worldwide. The Ads Media Planning team is at the heart of designing and delivering state-of-the-art media planning solutions that power Netflix ’s advertising business.

We are developing innovative, in-house ad tech systems that enable advertisers and internal partners to efficiently plan, allocate, and optimize media investments across Netflix ’s platform.

Our technology translates advertiser objectives into actionable media plans, ensuring seamless integration, automation, optimization, compliance, and management of media strategies at scale.

We work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver robust media planning capabilities that serve our advertisers, members, and Netflix ’s broader business goals. The Live Ads Management team is driving one of Netflix ’s most exciting frontiers — bringing advertising to Live Events.

We’re building the intelligence that powers ad experiences during some of Netflix ’s biggest real-time moments, from live sports to global specials. Our team develops smart, scalable capabilities that help ad operations plan, set up, and deliver ads seamlessly during live broadcasts.

We’re pushing the boundaries with automated manifest generation, machine learning–driven optimizations, and agentic workflows that adapt in real-time to maximize both monetization and viewer experience.

We work hand in hand with creative, streaming, and ads engineering teams to make advertising on Netflix Live feel effortless — blending storytelling, technology, and real-time decisioning into one unforgettable experience. It’s a fast-moving, high-visibility team shaping how live entertainment and advertising come together on a global stage.

The Ads Platform Foundations team builds the core platforms, frameworks, and shared services that accelerate development across the Ads organization. We focus on enabling teams to move faster and build consistently through scalable UI infrastructure, common components, and foundational workflows.

Our work also powers access control across domains and underpins core systems such as Public API, GenAI foundations, and the Ads Entity Service — a knowledge graph connecting all Ads entities. Together, we provide the technical backbone that drives consistency, reliability, and velocity across Ads.

The Ads Campaign Management team is responsible for our in-house Order Management System (OMS) used by our account managers to facilitate the booking and execution of advertising campaigns on behalf of Agencies, Brands, and Advertisers.

The team owns key parts of our campaign hierarchy (Orders, Line Items) and closely intersects with almost every other team across Ads Engineering (Creatives, Forecasting, Audiences, Measurement, Ad Serving, etc) as well as business teams across Account Management and Ad Operations to facilitate the set-up, execution, and monitoring of ads across the Netflix ecosystem.

The Ads Inventory Management & Forecasting team builds state-of-art real-time inventory forecasting solutions leveraging ML models and high-performance ad server simulations.

The team also builds systems that enable publisher inventory management solutions, which support various monetization strategies such as dynamic pricing, rate card management, product packaging, inventory split, and yield optimization. The Ads Data Clean Room team is redefining how clean rooms are used in digital advertising.

We’re building data collaboration tools as internal services, allowing multiple teams to share data with external partners in a convenient and privacy-safe way. Our scope extends beyond traditional clean room use cases to include novel integrations where data has traditionally been shared more openly.

As the ads data landscape evolves, our team will continue to lead by creating new ways to enable collaboration while protecting privacy.

The Ads Finance team ’s vision is to establish a compliant, accurate, automated, and omni-channel Finance and billing system that streamlines and optimizes financial operations for ads, with a core charter to create a unified and compliant Revenue Recognition layer, Automate billing, Invoicing and Journal processes.

The Ads Finance platform centralizes and validates all the raw data—from campaign performance to pricing structures—needed to calculate and bill our diverse advertising revenue streams.

This ensures financial integrity and consistency, providing a reliable foundation for all core Ad business operations, including budgeting, predicting future revenue, and managing credit and pricing strategies.

The Ads Eventing team builds and operates the foundational systems that collect, validate, enrich, and deliver ads-related events at a massive scale. These high-throughput data pipelines ingest raw signals from client devices (TV, mobile), server-side ad insertions, and external third-party integrations.

The core mission is to transform these raw signals into clean, reliable, and privacy-safe data streams, ensuring data quality and fidelity across the board.

This critical infrastructure directly powers all core downstream functions, including real-time ad serving decisions, robust measurement and attribution systems, and financial reconciliation and billing workflows. The Ads Reporting Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering the final, actionable data to stakeholders.

Their focus is on building the systems that consume validated and enriched ads delivery data to power the comprehensive reporting surfaces used by internal teams and advertisers to analyze campaign performance and business outcomes.

They ensure the data presented is accurate, timely, and easy to consume, enabling key functions like measurement and attribution analysis, financial reconciliation, and strategic decision-making based on business results. The Ads CRM team delivers the AI-powered Go-to-Market platform, the strategic engine for Netflix Ads sales and marketing.

We don't just collect customer data; we create a unified, enriched view of our customers and their ad spend across every source, managing the entire lifecycle for impeccable quality and completeness.

Our intuitive UI and intelligent automation agents surface critical, actionable insights, empowering our sales teams to cut through the noise, focus on high-value client engagements, and accelerate the success of Netflix Ads. The Human Agent Tooling team builds the software Chime's support agents use every day to help members. When a member has a problem a bot can't solve, a human agent picks it up — and the tools we build are what let that agent understand the member's situation, take the right action, and resolve the issue quickly and safely. That includes the agent workspace, case management, the systems that surface member context in real time, and the controls that govern what actions agents can take.
Our mission is to make every human support interaction faster, safer, and more effective. When our tools work well, agents resolve issues in fewer clicks and members get better answers — and we measure our success by both.
We're investing heavily in this platform: modernizing the agent experience, building safer and more granular access controls, and improving how agent tooling connects to the rest of Chime's systems. We work closely with Product, Operations, and the agents themselves to shape what great support tooling looks like.
The base salary offered for this role and level of experience will begin at $117,000.00 and up to $162,000.00. Full-time employees are also eligible for a bonus, competitive equity package, and benefits. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.
In this role, you can expect to
Agent workspace — Contribute to the tools agents use to view member context, manage cases, and take action. You'll build well-scoped features that make agents' day-to-day faster and less error-prone.
Member context and case data — Help build the systems that pull together the right information about a member and surface it to the agent at the right moment.
Access controls and safety — Work on the permissions and guardrails that determine what actions agents can take on member accounts. These systems handle sensitive moments and need to be correct and reliable.
Integrations — Build and maintain the connections between agent tooling and the other Chime systems agents depend on, with support from your team.
Observability — Add logging, monitoring, and dashboards so we can see how tools are performing and catch issues early.
To thrive in this role, you have
Some professional software development experience (roughly 1+ years) or equivalent through internships, projects, or a strong CS foundation
Exposure to Ruby on Rails or a comparable web framework, or eagerness to learn it
Familiarity with working against a database
An appreciation for maintainable, well-tested code
A strong desire to learn and to dig into how things actually work

The data platform end to end: ingestion, storage, and the query paths that keep millions of records fast on screen. You design it, you build it, you run it in production.
The platform layer, directly with the CTO: infrastructure, deployments, and the path to production for the whole team.
Performance and correctness work in the optimization engine, together with our research engineers.
Your features from first line to production: nobody hands you a ticket and waits.
How we work
Small team, short lines of communication, no layers. You own your features end to end: you build them, you ship them to production yourself, you run them.
Feedback runs both ways and it runs continuously, in daily work and in weekly one-on-ones. We talk as equals. We communicate proactively and flag it early when something isn't working out. Saying no is part of the job.
We like this work, and you'll notice. The energy of a small team that cares is what people remember about being here. We review each other's code, and we like being together in the Cologne office, because the fastest conversations still happen in a room.

5+ years building production backend or data-intensive systems.
Strong Python and solid TypeScript, with the appetite to work in both daily.
Analytics-data experience: real SQL depth, plus any of Parquet/Arrow/DuckDB/dbt/warehouse internals.
Production PostgreSQL (multi-tenant, migrations, performance).
Data pipelines over heterogeneous sources (ERP exports, Excel, CSV) onto object storage (S3 or comparable), built to keep working as customers and formats grow.
Distributed systems and API design: typical failure modes, HTTP/auth/caching, sane versioning and error behavior.
Engineering craft: design patterns, CI/CD pipelines you set up yourself, prototypes you can throw away.
You have worked in a team, not mostly alone, and you know from experience which agile practices carry their weight.
You have experience working with Linear, Jira, or a similar project management tool.
You communicate proactively, too much rather than too little, and you organize yourself and your work.
German at C1 or better, and fluent English. Team life runs in German; code and docs are English.
NRW-based (Cologne office), optionally Munich, Stuttgart, Berlin area or else willing to work hybrid. Open to find a way if we fit.
Nice to have: a substantial migration you carried out end to end (system, stack, or data) · telemetry and observability · Cloudflare or comparable serverless infrastructure · frontend experience, ideally with Solid.js or another reactive framework · optimization/OR exposure · manufacturing or ERP data experience.
You are structured and biased for action, and you have shown you play to win wherever life has put you so far.
This role is not for you if you want a clearly defined box, or work handed to you in tickets. We are a small team, pre-Series A: structures and processes are still being built, by us and by you. Priorities shift with customers, and some weeks a deadline bends the plan.

Impact. You see your results in the real world, fast. The problems are concrete (production plans, capacities, logistics), and customers can measure in euros what your work changed.
Ownership. What you build, you ship, and you own it once it runs. No layers between you and production, no approval chain that turns your decision into someone else's.
The people next to you. You work directly with the CTO on the platform layer and with our research engineers on the optimization engine, and you build on eye level with the founders.
Shaping. You shape how this team works, not just what it builds. The processes are still forming, and whoever shows up with a better way of doing things gets to install it. This is a place for system thinkers: the interesting part isn't writing the code, it's seeing how the pieces fit and where they'll break. The company is early; your scope will grow with it.
Feedback speed. You will know directly what you are up to, we speak out loud, we adjust, we grow. Together.
High stakes. Competitive salary and relevant room in the equity package (VSOP) to match your contribution and your career development.
The basics. Hardware of your choice · AI tooling budget · sports membership · Deutschland-Ticket.
Process: first conversation, 20 minutes, with me or with the engineer who owns our frontend. Second conversation with the two of us together; this is where the technical questions get deep. Then a hands-on challenge, about three hours of your time, followed by a 45-minute walkthrough where you explain your solution and the decisions behind it.

Finally, the team: online first, then in person at the office. Both sides decide. Two to three weeks end to end, and you hear back within days after each step. Before you decide, ask us to put you on a call with someone who will tell you the good, the bad and the ugly.
To apply: skip the cover letter. Tell us about your favorite system you have built, and one decision in it, you would reverse today.
"Hustle the day, analyze at night, reinforce something outstanding." Period.

Who we are
Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched. Tables run every clinical trial, every financial model, every scientific experiment, every business decision, and no one had built a foundation model that truly understood them.
Until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables. The next modality shift in AI is happening, and we're hiring the team that makes it.
Momentum. We pioneered tabular foundation models and are now the world-leading organization in structured-data ML. Our TabPFN v2 model was published as a Nature cover story and set a new state of the art for tabular machine learning.

Since release we've scaled model capabilities 20x+, passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and are seeing accelerating adoption across research and industry - from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi to improving clinical-trial decisions with BostonGene .
The hardest work is ahead. We're scaling tabular foundation models to millions of rows, thousands of features, real-time inference, and entirely new data modalities, while building the infrastructure to run them in production across some of the most demanding industries on earth. These are open problems no one else is working on at this level.
Our team. We're a small, highly selective team of 30+ engineers, researchers, and GTM specialists, with backgrounds spanning Google, Apple, Amazon, DeepMind, Meta, Microsoft Research, G-Research, Jane Street, Goldman Sachs, and CERN. We're led by Frank Hutter , Noah Hollmann , and Sauraj Gambhir , and advised by world-leading AI researchers including Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. We ship fast, do top-tier research, and hold each other to an extremely high bar.
What's next. In 2025 we raised €9m pre-seed led by Balderton Capital, backed by leaders from Hugging Face, DeepMind, and Black Forest Labs. The next phase of growth is here, which makes this an ideal time to join.

At Ping Identity , we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.
Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.
While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.
We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity , we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.
We are seeking a hands-on Principal Software Engineer to build PingOne Privilege, our cloud-native Zero Trust privileged access platform, and the AI security capabilities that protect how enterprises adopt agentic AI. This is a coding role — you will design, ship, and own production systems alongside the rest of the team. Key Responsibilities:

Build the Platform: Design and ship core services for PingOne Privilege, our cloud-native platform in Go — just-in-time access, credential-less authentication, and Zero Trust access to multi-cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) and on-prem resources.

Agentic AI Security: Build our AI security capabilities hands-on — MCP gateways, AI agent identity and governance, and real-time guardrails that detect and block prompt injection and data exfiltration.

Distributed Systems: Develop highly available, multi-region services on Kubernetes with durable workflow orchestration and distributed data stores, and own them through design, implementation, and production.

Identity & Access Protocols: Implement deep integrations with identity protocols (OAuth2/OIDC, SAML, SCIM, certificate-based auth) and build secure proxy and gateway layers for SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, databases, and web applications.

Technical Leadership: Raise the bar through code reviews and design reviews, mentor engineers by working alongside them, and set the example for high-quality, secure, maintainable code.

Experience: 10+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with 4+ years at a Principal or Staff level building large-scale security or identity products — as an individual contributor who writes and ships production code daily.

Security & Identity Expertise: Deep working knowledge of IAM/PAM — privileged access, secrets and key management, session brokering, least-privilege and Zero Trust architectures — with hands-on depth in OAuth2/OIDC and PKI.

Tech Stack: Expert-level proficiency in Go (or strong systems-language background with willingness to work in Go), Cloud Native technologies (AWS/Azure/GCP, Kubernetes), and distributed data stores (Cassandra or similar NoSQL); experience with workflow engines (e.g., Temporal) a plus.

AI Systems (preferred): Experience building or securing LLM-based systems — agent frameworks, MCP, model-based threat detection, or AI guardrails.

Leadership: Influence through code and design, not title — proven ability to drive cross-team technical decisions while staying in the critical path of delivery.
Education: BS/MS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day.

LLM post-training and reinforcement learning

As a first-tier supplier to our renowned business partner **Roche Diagnostics in Rotkreuz**, we are currently looking for a motivated and dedicated **Linux System Engineer** for a temporary assignment of 12 months, with possibility of extension.
Roche has a specialized team of software and hardware experts at the heart of their medical instrument development. They build and own "Roche Linux", a purpose-built, Debian-based platform that powers the next generation of medical devices.

The company is seeking a senior engineer to join this team, someone who combines deep technical mastery with a passion for craftsmanship and a relentless drive to make things better.

In this role, you will be a core contributor and consultant, ensuring the foundational operating system is robust, secure, and perfectly tailored to the demanding world of MedTech.
The perfect candidate is a systems thinker who effortlessly grasps the big picture and understands how individual components interact to form a cohesive, reliable whole.

Driven by an innate curiosity, you are never satisfied with surface-level explanations; instead, you are a pragmatic problem-solver who uses a logical, structured mindset to independently track down root causes.

Rather than waiting for direction, you are a proactive contributor who spots areas for improvement and takes the initiative to elevate the entire team.

Finally, you are an excellent communicator with advanced English skills, fully capable of translating complex technical concepts into clear insights for both engineering peers and non-technical stakeholders alike.

* Architect and Engineer the Core OS Platform: Take ownership of the custom Debian-based distribution. This includes everything from kernel customization and driver integration to the creation, maintenance, and optimization of Debian packages.
* Master the Build and Release Pipeline: Evolve and improve the infrastructure and processes used to build, test, and release the Linux distribution, ensuring reliability and reproducibility.
* Be the Ultimate Escalation Point: Act as the go-to expert for complex, low-level system issues. Perform deep-dive troubleshooting, debugging, and root-cause analysis across both software and hardware.
* Consult and Empower Development Teams: Guide internal project teams on how to best leverage the Roche Linux platform.
* Proactively Drive Improvement: Constantly seek out opportunities to enhance the distribution, tools, and processes. Whether it's improving system performance, strengthening security, or automating a complex workflow, you will be expected to identify needs and champion solutions.
### Must-Haves ###
* Deep, Hands-On Linux Mastery (10+ years): You are a seasoned professional who is comfortable across the entire Linux stack.
* Custom Distribution Engineering: Proven, extensive experience building, modifying, or maintaining a customized Linux distribution, with a strong preference for Debian (e.g., using tools like debootstrap, molior, aptly).
* Expertise in Debian Packaging: You don't just apt-get install. You can create, patch, and maintain .deb packages from scratch, understanding policy, dependencies and best practices.
* Strong Scripting and Automation Skills: Fluency in Python and Shell scripting is essential for building tools and automating system tasks.
* Fundamental Systems Knowledge: A solid grasp of operating system theory (process management, memory, filesystems), software build systems (make, CMake), and the full testing and packaging lifecycle.
* Advanced English is mandatory; German is a welcome bonus.
### Nice-to-Haves ###
* Proficiency in a systems programming language like C or C++.
* Experience with embedded systems, the ARM platform, hardware drivers, and low-level hardware/software integration.
* Knowledge of modern infrastructure: Virtualization (KVM), Containers (Docker, Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines, and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform).
* Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS).

At VREY , we're building the EnergyOS for multi-family buildings .
Germany has over 3.3 million apartment buildings — and they are the blind spot of the energy transition. <1% solar penetration. <2% smart metering. Almost no flexibility or intelligent energy management.
At the same time, regulation is forcing property owners into major investment: solar is becoming mandatory, smart meters must be rolled out nationwide within five years, heating and mobility are electrifying. The apartment building is transforming from passive real estate into an active part of the decentralised energy infrastructure.
What's missing is an integrated system that makes this transition economically viable and operationally manageable.
VREY combines certified meter operation with proprietary software , enabling property owners to sell self-generated solar power directly to their tenants — simply, and without having to become an energy supplier themselves (§42b EnWG). Regulatory obligation becomes a profitable, predictable opportunity:
Double-digit returns and asset appreciation for owners,
~20% electricity cost savings for tenants, and
digital infrastructure for storage, heat pumps, and flexibility.
We already manage a three-digit number of projects — including some of Germany's largest property holders and housing cooperatives — in all 16 federal states. In the course of our seed financing, we raised €3.3M from leading impact and energy VCs (including Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, and Kopa Ventures). We're now entering the next growth phase and expanding our team.
We're at the beginning of a structural market shift. Join us and help build the leading EnergyOS.
Your Profile
You have 2+ years of professional experience building and running full-stack web applications, ideally with Ruby on Rails . Experience in comparable frameworks (Django, Laravel, Spring Boot, NextJS) will also be considered, if you are truly motivated to learn and work with Rails.
You have a strong understanding and hands-on experience designing and optimizing relational database schemas (we use PostgreSQL ).
You are used to working with APIs and integrating with 3rd-party services.
You have solid experience setting up and maintaining cloud/server infrastructure. We have a basic Heroku setup and Github CI/CD and need to gradually scale and improve monitoring etc.
You have at least basic frontend development skills, ideally with solid fundamentals (HTML, CSS and JavaScript), as well as familiarity with both the Rails way (Hotwire, Turbo and Stimulus) and a framework like React or Vue.
You are actively working with AI and pushing for efficient agentic setups; we are establishing Claude Code in the team and the whole company.
You like to take ownership for the features and components you work on and you are proactive in the product development.
You are excited about startups and want to make a real impact on the product and the company in a truely agile way.
You are based in Berlin (or willing to relocate). You will enjoy working in our office in Friedrichshain with the team most of the time, with the flexibility of 1-2 remote work days a week.
You are willing to learn energy industry terms in English and German and being comfortable with some parts of the company operating mostly in German. (Team language is English.)
Nice to have: You have experience working with multi-tenancy systems and/or are experienced with payment provider integration (e.g., Stripe Connect)

You will be an early member of our growing product development team, working across the entire stack.
The core functionality of the VREY platform is processing smart meter measurement data for analyzing and billing solar power usage. For this purpose, we provide landlords and tenants with a portal and automate contract management, invoicing and payment flows. An admin interface and integration with internal tools enable the creation and management of projects by our operations team.
While working on features and integrations, you also help us improve our infrastructure and backend processes, enabling our platform to scale.
1. Full-stack feature development
You co-design and build features across the full stack, from database to UI.
You work directly with product management, design and internal users to get the details right.
You ensure that our features perform well for a growing number of users.
2. Data processing, automation and reliability
You co-own the development of our crucial backend processes: importing and processing of smart meter measurement data and automated billing.
You help designing and maintaining the underlying server infrastructure.
You instrument, optimize and monitor critical processes so they remain fast, reliable and dependable as we scale.
3. Technical design, architecture and engineering excellence
You research, evaluate and design technical solutions to new problems together with the team.
You contribute to our aspiration to get better and more efficient as engineers and as a team every day.
You continuously improve our development environment and engineering processes, including adopting the right tools, workflows and AI-powered development practices.

Competitive salary including shares based on the level of your experience.
Real ownership: You shape VREY actively from day one. Ownership means responsibility for your tasks end-to-end and the opportunity to take leadership.
Visible impact: We ship features every day that make a difference for our customers and colleagues.
Personal and professional growth: We have very skilled and experienced people on the team that you can learn from and we actively provide opportunities to develop your career.
Making a difference: Our daily work reduces energy costs for tenants, advances the energy transition in residential buildings, and accelerates the economic decarbonisation of Germany's housing stock.
Great workplace: Office in a cool co-working space in Berlin-Friedrichshain, with free drinks, cerials, fruits, and plenty of lunch options nearby.
We're a team that shares lunch, swaps ideas, welcomes new faces regularly, and genuinely listens — come help shape what comes next.

Taktile empowers financial institutions to transform into truly AI-native organizations. We’re growing rapidly with enterprise customers across banks and insurance companies, and we’re looking for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to join our Platform team.

Our Engineering and Product Design teams are building multiple verticals on our platform at high speed, leveraging AI and building agentic functionality into the platform itself. As we scale into the world's largest regulated financial institutions, identity and access management (IAM), authorization, and fine-grained permissions have become foundational to our enterprise readiness.
We are hiring a Full-Stack Engineer to join the team building Taktile's IAM and permissions platform : the authorization backbone that powers enterprise-grade access control across our product.
Joining us, you'll design and build permission models and access controls end-to-end, from the React/TypeScript access-management and admin UIs down to the Python (FastAPI) authorization services. You'll take on the problems that make enterprise authorization genuinely hard: multi-tenant isolation , fine-grained permission checks in the hot path of millions of decisions a day, audit and access trails , and the constraints of regulated financial services .

Design, build, and operate core authorization primitives such as roles, policies, and fine-grained permission checks (RBAC/ReBAC), along with the authentication and SSO/OAuth/OIDC flows that sit on top of them.
Guarantee strict multi-tenant isolation so every customer's data and decisions stay fully segregated.
Keep fine-grained permission checks fast in the hot path of millions of automated decisions per day, where both latency and correctness are non-negotiable.
Build audit and access-trail capabilities that give customers and auditors a verifiable record of who accessed what, when, and why.
Design for regulated-industry constraints (financial services, SOC 2 / ISO 27001, data residency), where access control is a compliance requirement, not just a feature.
Leverage leading edge AI tools (e.g. Claude) on a daily basis to build industry-shaping AI-native capabilities.

Strong proficiency with React and TypeScript.
Experience building access control systems, with exposure to authentication and authorization concepts (RBAC, SSO, OAuth/OIDC, multi-tenant permissions).
Strong engineering fundamentals with a passion for simplicity and precision.

Fluency in English, both written and spoken, is essential as we operate in a remote environment requiring clear and effective communication.

Prior ops or on-call experience.
